Braised Red Cabbage for St. Martin's Day

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag)

Serves 6-8Prep 25 minCook 1 hour 30 min

Braised red cabbage is a classic side dish, especially popular in Germany and Austria, often accompanying roasted meats like goose or duck. For St. Martin's Day, celebrated on November 11th, it's a traditional accompaniment to the festive Martinmas Goose, offering a sweet and tangy contrast to the rich poultry. Its vibrant color also adds a beautiful touch to the holiday table.

Ingredients

  • 1 medium head red cabbage (about 2.5 lbs / 1.1 kg), cored and thinly sliced
  • 2 tablespoons (30g) butter or duck fat
  • 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped
  • 2 medium tart apples (like Granny Smith), peeled, cored, and grated or finely diced
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) apple cider vinegar
  • 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar (or to taste)
  • 1 cup (240ml) water or red wine
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 4-5 whole cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, freshly ground, or to taste

Method

  1. Core the red cabbage and slice it very thinly, or shred it using a food processor.
  2. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter or duck fat over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
  3. Add the thinly sliced red cabbage to the pot. Stir well to combine with the onions and fat. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage begins to wilt slightly.
  4. Stir in the grated or diced apples, apple cider vinegar, sugar, water (or red wine), bay leaves, and whole cloves. Season with salt and pepper.
  5. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot tightly and let it braise for at least 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the cabbage is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
  6. Check seasoning after about an hour; adjust sugar, vinegar, salt, and pepper to taste. The cabbage should be a balance of sweet and tart.
  7. Before serving, remove the bay leaves and whole cloves. Serve hot.

Tips

  • For a deeper flavor, replace water with a dry red wine.
  • A pinch of ground cinnamon or allspice can be added with the other spices for extra warmth.
  • This dish tastes even better the next day, making it perfect for preparing ahead of time.
